parsed.explanation: Combined regime: Sections 365/365A (up to 10 years, both sexes) are enforced mainly as a police lever. Police harassment, arrest-threat extortion, forced anal and vaginal examinations (condemned as torture), and ignored complaints are documented. Prosecutions are limited, and no capital exposure is documented. Custody placement defaults to birth sex with no dedicated trans housing; the ID-gated preference and doctor-assessment routes are discretionary. Foreign-document entry friction and visitor-facing care denial are not documented. Care access is hostile for residents, and no anti-discrimination protection exists. Official signals are mixed. Overall the state-directed policing and birth-sex custody default place this in the High Risk band, well below the reduced-risk tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No visitor entry or document-check friction is documented. Visitors carry home-issued documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Document checks could feed into police stops, but the dossier does not link entry to later detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police use arrest threats to assault, harass and extort LGBTQIA people. Forced anal and vaginal exams to seek evidence of same-sex conduct are documented and condemned as torture. Custody placement defaults to birth sex.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A doctor-assessment and ID-gated preference route exists, but it is discretionary, applies mainly to card-holders, and has no statutory basis.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor arrested under police discretion would likely face birth-sex placement, with the exam practice as a further exposure in custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National prison department states separate trans space is impossible in current prisons. Birth-sex ward system is the practical default.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Future prisons are proposed to have separate space, which is not yet in force.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The national policy applies uniformly; there is no subnational variation in the record.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming surgery is relatively inaccessible. Patients report ignorance, curiosity and ridicule, and some avoid public facilities. Hormone access is described as fraught.
care_services.protection: A 2016 circular allows gender recognition certificates, but this is resident-facing and is not a visitor protection.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care would meet the same hostile clinical environment; no visitor-specific emergency-care denial is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official bodies and police are the foremost perpetrators of anti-LGBTI violations. Officials cite sex-offence concerns to resist gender-based placement. One source notes vagrancy and personation provisions used against gender expression.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A head-of-state statement and a 2021 poll show partial official and public acceptance, but neither is operative protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The threat frame sits in the police and prison system, which is the traveller-facing layer.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penalties rise for offences involving minors, and family members seek conversion treatment for LGBTQ relatives. A visitor travelling with a minor could face placement or family-conduct scrutiny, but this is not documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor in a family arrested or detained would have no documented shield, and placement rules apply to the adult.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police routinely ignore complaints from LGBTQ victims of sexual violence or blackmail. No trans-specific violence rate is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Formal prosecutions of attackers are not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims who report face police indifference; the state response is itself a damning factor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No comprehensive anti-discrimination law. A 2016 human rights report and a 2023 opinion note that administrative circulars are insufficient. Prosecution data after 2012 is unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A national human rights commission has facilitated complaints; NGO and community infrastructure exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper, but the record shows little operative remedy against police.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest analogue: birth-sex custody with assaults, and a cross-dressing arrest statute used against visitors. This dossier has similar birth-sex placement and police-led harm, and adds documented forced anal exams. Its prosecutions are limited, with no capital exposure documented, so it sits near the 0.25 anchor.
Weekly raids, extortion by officers, and birth-sex-linked document rules. This dossier documents police extortion and arrest-threat assaults, but not raids, so it sits around the same tier.
Police stops and forced interviews with brief detention, with imprisonment rare. This dossier has more severe custody exposure (birth-sex placement and forced exams), so it sits below 0.35.
Detention with assault and withheld care, and capital provisions on the books. This dossier documents no capital or lethal custody outcomes and limited prosecutions, so it sits clearly above 0.15.

parsed.synthesis: Police are the documented core exposure, using the sexuality statute as a lever for arrest threats, extortion and forced exams. Custody defaults to birth sex, and the exception route is discretionary and ID-gated. Those custody rules reach any detained visitor. The record shows no capital outcomes and few prosecutions. Official acceptance statements and polls are partial mitigators, but no operative protection reaches visitors. Care is hostile, and complaints to police go unaddressed. The result is a High Risk rating, lower than the 0.35 anchors and close to the 0.25 anchors.
